summary: Draft candidate package for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power. The clean Win25H2Clean phase-0 batch confirmed the parent key exists while the value is absent on baseline, the repo power notes carry an exact docs hit with literal 1, the targeted current-build string batch found an exact ntoskrnl.exe Unicode hit, the shared mega-trigger runtime lane armed candidate value 1 but recovered without an exact hit, a retained local-KD disassembly pass shows the visible generic power-setting query/store layer operating through PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration, PopPowerSettingChangeStamp, and PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks rather than a visible registry API, and a wildcard KD plus symbol-seeded Ghidra follow-up shows no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` helper while the only naturally resolved setting callback is the timeout-specific `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`. New retained live-state and direct-reader passes now confirm `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired = 1` and show `PopPowerRequestEvaluateExecutionRequiredStatus` reading that global on the current build. A retained broad lightweight runtime lane also wrote the pair from baseline-missing to candidate value `1`, completed a real soft reboot, and still returned `no-hit` for the pair after reboot. A new retained retry audit over 10 mega-trigger runtime runs shows the pair repeatedly armed from baseline-missing to `1` and then exited `aborted-recovered` with zero exact hits on every parsed retry. A retained runtime path audit over the only current-build `path-hits.csv` capture found zero exact hits for the pair itself but 15 adjacent `Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` accesses by `svchost.exe`, a new override-alignment audit ties those adjacent hits to the already-proven current-build override lineage, and a new power-setting trace-callback audit shows the visible generic setter registering `PopTracePowerSettingChange` rather than an exact pair-specific callback. A new KVM guest-control audit then showed the dedicated narrow runtime runner is already wired, but the active libvirt guest lacks a qemu guest agent channel, the repo controller stack is still vmrun-backed, and the attached bootstrap ISO path is missing on the host checkout. The candidate remains research-only because the earlier Control\Power seeding path and an exact post-boot read are still unresolved, and the live runtime-trace lane is currently environment-gated rather than runner-missing.

validation_proof.notes: The repo power notes provide the exact candidate name, literal value, and intended symbol mapping, but they do not by themselves prove current-build runtime seeding semantics.

setting.name: Allow Audio To Enable Execution Required Power Requests
setting.casual_explanation: This low-level Control\Power value appears to influence whether active audio can contribute to execution-required power-request behavior inside the kernel power-request subsystem.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track it when they want to understand how audio activity participates in execution-required power requests and whether that behavior is registry-seeded or runtime-driven.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The candidate now has enough docs, static, and debugger evidence for a real draft package, and the visible current-build live state plus direct reader path are no longer open questions. A retained broad soft-reboot lane also exists, but it only narrows the missing layer to exact post-boot tracing rather than proving an exact rebooted read. The only retained runtime path-hit CSV currently lands on the adjacent `PowerRequestOverride` subtree rather than on the pair itself, that adjacent subtree now has its own override-lineage alignment proof, and the visible generic setter path now has explicit trace-callback proof rather than pair-binding proof.
setting.professional_notes: The Win25H2Clean 96-key phase-0 existence batch confirmed that HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power exists while AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests itself is absent on the clean baseline. Repo power notes document an exact literal of 1 and map the setting to PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired. The targeted string batch on the current build found an exact Unicode hit in C:\Windows\System32\ntoskrnl.exe for the value name. A shared mega-trigger runtime lane then armed candidate value 1 for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests but the Procmon export recovered in an aborted state and did not yield an exact read. The retained local-KD power-setting query/store pass disassembled PopQueryPowerSettingUlong, PopGetPowerSettingValue, and PopSetPowerSettingValue. In the retained path, the generic power-setting subsystem acquires PopSettingLock, resolves configuration objects through PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration, updates PopPowerSettingChangeStamp, walks PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks, schedules PopSetNotificationWork, and contains an explicit callback registration site that loads `PopTracePowerSettingChange` into `r8` before calling `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`. That retained callsite reinforces that the visible generic setter path is still notification/trace plumbing rather than an exact binding site for the execution-required pair. A second retained wildcard KD pass then showed no visible `nt!*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbols on the current build and only one `nt!*PowerRequest*Setting*` symbol: PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback. The symbol-seeded Ghidra probe on that callback resolved only the timeout GUID path and found no direct or bounded indirect references to the callback symbol itself. New retained local-KD live-state proof now shows `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired = 1`, matching the repo-doc enabled literal. A retained disassembly pass also shows `PopPowerRequestEvaluateExecutionRequiredStatus` directly comparing `PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired` against zero while it reads `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` during execution-required evaluation. A retained broad lightweight runtime lane then armed both execution-required values from baseline-missing to candidate value `1`, completed a real `reboot_mode=soft` cycle with healthy shell state before and after reboot, and still reported `no-hit` for both pair members in the post-boot batch result. The only retained current-build runtime `path-hits.csv` capture for this lane also stays adjacent: it contains zero exact hits for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests and AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests, but 15 `svchost.exe` accesses under `HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` covering the root, `Driver`, `Process`, and `Service` subkeys. A new alignment audit then ties those adjacent hits back to the already-proven override family in wildcard KD evidence: `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestOverrideQueryResponse`, `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize`, `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery`, and `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideCleanup`, while the retained root dump also contains the `PowerRequestOverride` subtree. Together these follow-ups close the visible live-state and direct-reader gaps, while narrowing the runtime-trace story to an adjacent override lineage and a trace-oriented generic setter rather than exact pair reads. A new host-side KVM guest-control audit then showed the remaining runtime lane is environment-gated: both execution-required records already map to the dedicated narrow path-aware runner, but that runner and the controller stack remain vmrun-backed, the live libvirt domain has no qemu guest agent channel, `guest-ping` fails with `QEMU guest agent is not configured`, and the domain XML still points at a missing `dist/regprobe-kvm-bootstrap.iso` path on the host checkout. If this candidate is still registry-backed on the current build, the Control\Power seeding must occur earlier than the visible generic query/store, trace-callback, timeout-setting, direct reader, and adjacent override layers, or the post-boot window must be captured from a restored guest-control surface with a narrower exact-read lane.

decision.why: AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests now has exact repo-doc coverage, clean-baseline absence proof, current-build ntoskrnl string corroboration, a real trigger arm, retained local-KD proof that `PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired = 1`, a direct current-build reader in `PopPowerRequestEvaluateExecutionRequiredStatus`, a retained local-KD view of the generic power-setting query/store layer, retained wildcard/symbolized binding follow-ups, a retained broad soft-reboot runtime lane that still returns `no-hit` after reboot, a retained retry audit showing 10 mega-trigger runtime attempts all ending `aborted-recovered`, a retained path audit showing only adjacent `PowerRequestOverride` activity in the visible runtime CSV layer, a new alignment audit that ties that adjacent subtree back to the current-build override family, a new trace-callback audit showing the visible generic setter registering `PopTracePowerSettingChange` rather than an exact pair binding, and a new host-side KVM guest-control audit showing the remaining narrow runtime lane is currently blocked by environment shape rather than by missing repo plumbing. The record remains draft because the visible current-build story is still callback-, timer-, override-, trace-, and in-memory-state driven, while the earlier Control\Power seeding path into that state and any exact rebooted read remain unresolved.
blocking_issues: The visible generic power-setting query/store layer is in-memory and callback-driven, but the earlier Control\Power seeding path into PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration objects or execution-required globals is still unresolved.

The only naturally resolved setting callback is tied to GUID_EXECUTION_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TIMEOUT and PopExecutionRequiredTimeout rather than to an exact AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests binding site.
A retained broad soft-reboot lane now exists, but it still produced only batch-level `no-hit` rather than an exact post-boot read for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests.

A retained retry audit over 10 mega-trigger runtime attempts shows the trigger family is no longer missing; it repeatedly arms the pair from baseline-missing to `1` but still exits `aborted-recovered` without an exact registry read for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests.

The only retained current-build runtime `path-hits.csv` capture shows adjacent `Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` accesses by `svchost.exe` and zero exact path hits for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests itself.

A retained alignment audit now links those adjacent runtime hits to the visible current-build override family rather than to an exact execution-required pair read, which strengthens the case that the missing layer is earlier seeding or a narrower exact-read lane.
A retained trace-callback audit shows the visible generic `PopSetPowerSettingValue` callback registration targets `PopTracePowerSettingChange`, not an exact execution-required pair binding site.

The dedicated narrow runtime lane is already mapped, but the active KVM session has no qemu guest agent channel, the repo controller stack still assumes vmrun, and the attached bootstrap ISO path is missing on the host checkout, so exact runtime capture is currently environment-gated.
